title: Cole (1903) · live unit-type trial
description: A mathematical journal excerpt in a single-column layout. Page 1 finishes a preceding article and begins F. N. Cole's article; page 4 finishes Cole's article and begins an article by Arnold Emch. The articles combine prose, displayed mathematics and page-bottom footnotes.

flows.main: Article titles, authorship and meeting information, prose, displayed mathematics and closing affiliations.
flows.notes: Footnotes printed below a rule at the foot of the page.

article.description: A journal article grouping its title, byline, meeting statement, numbered sections or body text, displayed mathematics and closing affiliation. Contains article_title, byline, meeting_statement, numbered_section, paragraph, display_formula, numerical_series and closing_affiliation.

numbered_section.description: A numbered division of an article, introduced by an inline Arabic numeral rather than a separate heading. Contains paragraph, display_formula and numerical_series.

article_title.description: The displayed title of an article.

byline.description: The displayed author credit following an article title.

meeting_statement.description: A parenthetical statement identifying the meeting and date at which an article was read.

paragraph.description: Running mathematical prose, including continuations interrupted by displayed mathematics or page breaks.

display_formula.description: A separately displayed equation or group of equations, including equation numbers where printed.

numerical_series.description: A displayed sequence of numerical values or products presented as mathematical data rather than prose.

closing_affiliation.description: An institutional affiliation and date printed at the end of an article.

footnote.description: A page-bottom note keyed to a symbol in the article; notes include bibliographic references and substantive remarks.

running_header.description: The running article title and date fragments at the top of the page.

page_number.description: The printed journal page number in the top margin.

ornament.description: An unlabelled decorative divider between articles.

relations.footnote_reference: Links a printed symbol in article text to the corresponding page-bottom footnote; distinguish repeated symbols by page and context.
relations.equation_reference: Links a prose reference such as equations (1) and (2) to the corresponding numbered displayed equations.

footnote_marker.description: A symbol such as * or † marking a footnote reference or the start of its note.

equation_label.description: A parenthesized identifier attached to a displayed equation, such as (1).

conventions: Transcribe in Unicode NFC, preserving printed spelling, capitalization, punctuation, diacritics and digits; do not silently modernize.
Preserve mathematical symbols, superscripts, subscripts, equation labels and meaningful arrangement as faithfully as the transcription format permits.
Keep the printed section numerals with their sections and retain footnote symbols at both references and notes.
Join prose split by page breaks according to its textual continuity, without treating running headers or page numbers as article text.
English is the principal language; French, German and Latin occur in cited titles. Preserve those titles in their printed languages.
The displayed-equation type covers both numbered and unnumbered equations; retain any printed labels individually.

discovery.rendering: PNG at 150 dpi, capped at the scan's own resolution
